markerIdentity: Codex independent AI physics marker B, K4 bilingual packet v2
independenceStatement: First-hand blind assessment of the designated packet. I saw the pupil-facing item, rubric, submissions and actual raster images. I did not consult an author key, previous marking, other reviewer or reconciliation. Scores below are my markings of synthetic submissions.
releaseDecision: The learner-facing assessment and its total-score rule are suitable for the stated introductory skill. The blind-case set needs two small corrections before claiming consistent case content and exact independent boundary scores for this edition.
stimulusInspection: In the 720 by 420 pixel stimulus, the point centres are at x=70 and 610, the 0,1,2,3 ruler marks at x=70,250,430,610. The arrowhead faces right at B, with its point obscured by the B dot. Its drawn length is three centimetres. The separate x and v keys show 1 m/cm and 2 (m/s)/cm. This gives 6 m/s. For the changed velocity scale only, the expected drawing spans 2/3 of the A–B separation and ends 1 drawn cm short of B. The coincidence at B in I is deliberately tested by changing the scale in II.

drawingInspection.R01: A=290, B=650 px; 120 px/cm. Rightward head at 530, so 2 cm from A. Both legends correct; label v_A.
drawingInspection.R02: Same positions, labels, keys and 2 cm line as R01, no head. Label v_A says whose quantity it is.
drawingInspection.R03: A=290, B=650; head at 590, 2.5 cm right of A. Both legends correct.
drawingInspection.R04: 2 cm right of A, normal positions. The v legend reads 3 m where the task calls for 3 m/s.
drawingInspection.R05: Arrow starts at B (650), head at 890, 2 cm rightwards. Its v_A label conflicts with S14 explicitly assigning it to B.
drawingInspection.R06: Arrow starts at A (290) and points to 50, exactly 2 cm to its left. B is 3 cm to the right of A.
drawingInspection.R07: Its own ruler spans 120 px for 3 cm; A=120, B=240, head=840. Arrow crosses B, is 18 cm and points right. Both keys correct.
drawingInspection.R08: A=290, B=650, rightward arrow from 338 to 578. Origin is 0.4 cm right of A, length is 2 cm, tip is 0.6 cm short of B. Generic v.
drawingInspection.R09: 2 cm horizontal line joining the A point and the 2-cm abscissa. No head; generic v. Equal to R02 in geometry with a different label.
drawingInspection.R10: 1 cm arrow from A=290 to x=410, rightwards. B=650. Both keys are correct.

findings: Physics and level: using a single named velocity relative to the ground, small whole-number scales and a built-in ruler is appropriate after introductory velocity and proportional scaling. The second drawing tests transfer. The comparison distinguishes a graphical endpoint from a claim about contact or future position.

Chat assessability: evidence is the learner’s actual drawing (e.g. uploaded photo or digital image with a usable ruler/grid) plus their computation and explanation. This assesses the single stated read/draw skill in the velocity example. Neither a host upload run nor transfer to other vector types was tested here.

Threshold: For each A–D, with no core and at most its supplement, the other three can contribute at most 12. Thus at most 13/16, below 13.5. With the entire performance scored 0, at most 12. This ensures some substantive evidence in each performance, not all subpoints in each. With a correct drawing, calculation, reasoned prediction and invariance but no explanation of tip meaning S03 earns 13; S20 with no answer to part 3 earns 12.

Small slips: a single wrong terminal unit in S02, one wrong legend in S10, one absent head with independent direction in S11, and one wrong quotient consistently reused in S13 each cost 0.5 once. S05 contains two independent slips. S07 and S12 give the frame but lack independent rightward direction and the head, so cannot take the slip allowance. S14–S16 earn follow-through credit outside the criterion with the maintained error.

Case S06 (DE and EN): the writer states that the quantity is a property of its carrier but does not give the inferential step “therefore the arrow starts at that carrier”. R08 is unanchored. I require that step for the explicit A supplement, so give A0. A pragmatic reader could credit the first sentence alone and award A1. Both yield failure (12 or 13). To test precisely supplement-only A, append “Deshalb soll er an seinem Träger beginnen.” / “That is why it should start at its carrier.” Retain omission of the specific carrier and R08.

Case S14 (DE and EN): R05 says v_A above a line originating at B while the text expressly insists on B. The maintained carrier-at-tip rule settles A=0, with no secondary penalty, so the grade is determinate. To give the drawing and text one consistent mistaken model, label the drawn arrow v or v_B.

Optional clarity for actual learners: Part 1 gives the stationary-ground frame, then asks which way. B rewards explicitly naming the frame. Asking learners to name the given reference frame when they state direction would make the supplementary point fully visible in the prompt.
I found no language-dependent grade. The one potentially reader-dependent case is S06. Agreement with any other independent marker requires separate reconciliation.
